as-01-action-service.designIntro: A representative uses an existing support application to explain a damaged order, then safely proposes a refund. Case C17 is the support case, order O4 is the purchase and r17 will identify one logical credit operation; these are fictional record identifiers, not Claude concepts.
as-01-action-service.deliveryIntro: Translate this design into tested implementation, approved processing and a measured pilot. The following are design choices to verify, not a claim that a deployment or business outcome already happened.
overviewRoute: Read the customer request and permitted order evidence
Separate a read-only answer from a proposed financial action
Validate arguments and enforce identity, ownership and approval policy
Execute once, reconcile observed status and hand unresolved work to staff
foundationDecisions: Entry point
Backend Messages API integration within the existing support application. The model proposes; application code owns the workflow.
Capability features
Start with grounded explanation and narrowly described client tools. Add writes only with deterministic authorization, validation and recovery.
Model
Compare approved candidates on tool selection, argument correctness, honest status reporting, latency and cost—not confidence alone.
Context
Supply permitted order/policy evidence and observed tool results. A typed account ID is untrusted input, not authenticated identity.

designReviewQuestions.title: Choose the authorization and tool-result boundary
designReviewQuestions.context: The backend receives an authenticated support session and an untrusted message naming order O4 and account A9. The assistant can propose lookup_order or issue_credit. Order ownership and current credit policy reside in business services.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which dispatch design best prevents an unauthorized credit while retaining a correct client-tool interaction?
options: Validate issue_credit arguments against input_schema, execute the payment, then compare the returned order owner with the account in the user message before displaying the result.

Derive the principal from the trusted session, validate tool arguments, load authoritative ownership/policy and authorize the exact action before execution; correlate the observed outcome to the assistant call using tool_use_id.
Have the model call lookup_order before issue_credit and treat its subsequent choice of the write tool as evidence that ownership and policy were satisfied.
Authorize the initial conversation once, bind it to the account in the message, and allow later schema-valid credit calls within that conversation without repeating action-level checks.
explanations: Schema validity does not establish entitlement. Checking after payment is too late, and the message account is not trusted identity.
The application checks identity, argument semantics and current action authority before the side effect; tool_use_id correlates the observed result but does not itself authorize execution.
Reading ownership evidence helps interpretation, but model tool selection is not an application-enforced authorization decision.
Conversation authorization does not establish current permission for each changed order, amount or policy condition. The principal must come from trusted identity.

designReviewQuestions.title: Reconcile a timed-out credit without duplicating it
designReviewQuestions.context: The authorized request for USD120 uses logical operation r17. The payment service times out after accepting the submission. The provider supports lookup by a persisted idempotency key. No receipt has reached the backend.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which recovery sequence most directly preserves correct financial state?
options: Return a tool_result with is_error=true, create r18 and retry the credit immediately because an errored model continuation cannot represent a completed payment.
Reuse r17 in the model prompt and let the assistant decide whether to retry from the likelihood that the provider received the request.

Persist r17 and its provider key as outcome unknown; query authoritative operation status, record any observed receipt and retry only under the provider’s idempotency contract; retain pending escalation if status cannot be established.
Treat the missing receipt as failure, remove r17 from the operation ledger and replay the original issue_credit tool_use so the next response has a clean history.
explanations: A tool-result error describes observed failure information; it does not prove the payment did not execute. A new logical key can duplicate the credit.
A prompt identifier does not provide durable deduplication or authoritative settlement status. Probability is not business evidence.
This retains the unknown state and uses the provider’s actual status/idempotency semantics. No new credit or success claim is inferred from the timeout.
Deleting the unknown operation loses recovery evidence. Replaying a proposal does not establish whether its prior side effect occurred.

as-02-document-pipeline.designIntro: A clerk uploads invoices for intake, not payment. The first invoice, EL-8, is a fictional source record containing USD84.50 and no purchase-order number. The application must decide which extracted records can enter the receiving system and what happens to each failed file.
as-02-document-pipeline.deliveryIntro: Translate this design into tested implementation, approved processing and a measured pilot. The following are design choices to verify, not a claim that a deployment or business outcome already happened.
overviewRoute: Accept a file and propose fields from its evidence
Validate the receiving contract and source meaning
Record a separate outcome for every file
Retry transient failures, quarantine unreadable sources and version acceptance rules
foundationDecisions: Entry point
Backend batch/queue worker calling the approved model API; a file is a distinct tracked unit.
Capability features
Extract a draft with a declared receiving schema; add validation and per-source outcome tracking, not an autonomous payment agent.
Model
Compare exact fields, missing-value handling and failure classification on representative files, then latency and cost.
Context
Supply the actual authorized file plus receiving contract/version. A filename or terminal API status is not accepted invoice evidence.

integration.why: Syntax is only one check; meaning, units and required fields must match the receiver.
integration.setup: Compare total_minor and purchase_order with the declared contract and source.
integration.repair: Reject 84.5 cents and the omitted key; use 8450 cents and explicit null only because the source supports them.
integration.proof: Receiver accepts only the corrected, validated contract; model completion is not acceptance.

fluencyLayers.plain: Clear PDF, unreadable scan and transient API failure need different outcomes.

integration.why: Responsible operation preserves successful work and explains each failure.

integration.repair: Track stable source IDs, validate successes, quarantine unreadable input and retry only eligible transient failures within limits.

designReviewQuestions.title: Choose the receiving validation contract
designReviewQuestions.context: Invoice EL-8 states USD84.50 and has no purchase-order number. Contract v1 requires total_minor to be an integer number of cents and purchase_order to be present as a string or null. The model returns {"total_minor":84.5}.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which receiving sequence best preserves the source meaning and the declared handoff contract?
options: Parse the JSON, round total_minor to the nearest integer and omit purchase_order because no value appeared on the source.

Use a supported structured-output schema when available, then validate the result against contract v1 and source units; reject the current draft and permit bounded correction to 8450 cents with purchase_order:null from the supplied evidence.
Accept the draft if the model response completed normally; convert dollars to cents only in the downstream payment formatter so intake remains schema-independent.
Change purchase_order to optional and total_minor to a general number for this request, preserving the original output as the new schema example.
explanations: Rounding produces 84 or 85 cents rather than USD84.50, and omitting the key violates this v1 contract. Source absence does not authorize schema changes.
Structure can constrain shape, while receiving validation separately checks units and evidence. The correction is justified by the stated source and explicit nullable contract.
Model completion is not receiving acceptance. Deferring unit interpretation allows invalid records through and this intake scenario does not authorize payment.
A receiver contract is a versioned agreement, not something inferred from a malformed instance. Broadening it here conceals the unit and missing-key defects.

designReviewQuestions.title: Recover a partially processed invoice folder
designReviewQuestions.context: The source ledger shows doc-A accepted under contract v1, doc-B unreadable, and doc-C failed with a transient service error before extraction. A consumer now proposes contract v2, where absent purchase_order may be omitted.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which processing plan best preserves useful work and a defensible acceptance history?
options: Resubmit all three files under v2, overwrite the v1 rows and count any completed model response as accepted so the folder has one consistent version.
Retry doc-B and doc-C with the same backoff policy, retain doc-A, and infer missing purchase-order values from earlier accepted invoices to avoid review.

Keep doc-A’s accepted v1 record; route doc-B for preparation/review, retry eligible doc-C within a budget, validate each returned draft and record the applicable contract version; test v1/v2 fixtures before changing future acceptance.
Migrate doc-A to v2 immediately by removing all null fields, quarantine every remaining failure permanently and report the folder complete because no requests remain running.
explanations: Reprocessing erases accepted history and repeats successful work. Terminal model responses still need schema and semantic validation.
Unreadable source data needs preparation or human resolution rather than an identical transport retry. Purchase-order evidence must not be borrowed or fabricated.
This separates error causes, preserves successful outcomes and provenance, and makes the contract change explicit without silently rewriting historic acceptance.
A contract allowing one absent field does not justify removing every null or rewriting history. No running requests is not equivalent to complete accepted coverage.

as-04-research-system.designIntro: A warehouse owner must choose one mobile-scanner pilot for next month. Glove usability, offline recovery, staff training and rollout feasibility all matter. The team investigates evidence rather than treating a polished recommendation as approval.
as-04-research-system.deliveryIntro: Translate this design into tested implementation, approved processing and a measured pilot. The following are design choices to verify, not a claim that a deployment or business outcome already happened.
overviewRoute: Name the warehouse decision and required evidence
Check returned claims and missing dimensions
Preserve gaps and let the accountable owner approve; simplify a later lookup
foundationDecisions: Entry point
A bounded research workflow owned by the application/coordinator; distinguish model delegation from automatic business approval.
Capability features
Start from supplied evidence. Add specialist investigation only for independent evidence needs, not to make the diagram impressive.
Model
Evaluate coverage, attribution, uncertainty and integration quality alongside elapsed time and cost.
Context
Each worker needs its own explicit goal, constraints and permitted sources; prior coordinator conversation is not implicit shared context.

designReviewQuestions.title: Define the specialist handoff contract
designReviewQuestions.context: A warehouse pilot must launch next month. The coordinator owns feasibility and training; proposed specialists investigate glove usability and offline recovery. Workers have isolated contexts and access only to their supplied permitted sources.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which assignment design best supports a complete, source-backed recommendation?
options: Pass each worker a specialty name and the coordinator’s conversation identifier; require valid JSON and let the final synthesis infer any omitted pilot constraints.

Give each worker the complete warehouse decision, relevant one-month and glove constraints, permitted sources and bounded specialty; require attributed claims, uncertainty and failure state, while the coordinator tracks every required dimension and owns synthesis.
Give every worker all available repository documents and ask each to choose the pilot independently; select the recommendation supported by the greatest number of matching responses.
Ask the coordinator to draft its final recommendation first, then request specialist JSON objects that confirm the selected device so the output schema remains consistent.
explanations: A conversation identifier does not transfer unseen context. Valid JSON does not supply missing constraints or establish complete evidence.
The brief makes each worker’s actual context and responsibility explicit. Attributed returns and dimension-level coverage let the coordinator integrate evidence and expose gaps.
Unbounded duplicated work increases noise and may expose irrelevant material. Agreement among generated recommendations is not evidence that all required dimensions were investigated.
Confirmation-first investigation can hide contrary or missing evidence. A consistent schema is not a substitute for independent findings and honest uncertainty.

designReviewQuestions.title: Finalize with a missing offline investigation
designReviewQuestions.context: Glove usability and training findings have source evidence. The connectivity worker times out. Its JSON envelope contains all required keys but offline recovery remains unknown. The pilot owner must decide whether next-month rollout is feasible.
designReviewQuestions.stem: Which finalization policy best preserves decision usefulness without concealing the failed investigation?
options: Accept the envelope because required keys are present, assign offline recovery the average confidence of the successful workers and mark the recommendation complete.
Discard all findings and rerun every specialist until their responses arrive together, then use response order to assemble the coverage report.

Preserve the supported findings, mark offline recovery unresolved in the dimension ledger, attempt a bounded targeted follow-up if justified, and give the owner the attributed evidence and explicit remaining feasibility risk if it stays unresolved.
Choose a device based on glove usability now and treat missing connectivity findings as an implementation task, since the coordinator has enough evidence to produce a fluent recommendation.
explanations: Presence of keys checks shape, not source-backed coverage. Averaged confidence cannot replace the missing connectivity evidence.
This discards valid work and response order does not establish assignment identity. Follow-up should target the missing requirement and preserve provenance.
This keeps partial success useful while making the missing required evidence and next owner visible. It does not pretend the pilot is approved.
Offline recovery is a stated feasibility requirement. Relabeling the unresolved requirement does not establish it or authorize launch.
